categories.title: Domain & service footprint
categories.lead: Follow domain references through code and configuration. A mention is a lead, not proof of ownership.

templates.title: Domain mentions in an organisation
templates.note: Find the scoped domain inside file contents.
templates.tip: Read surrounding lines before deciding what a reference means.

templates.title: Domain mentions in one repository
templates.note: Keep the investigation within one named project.
templates.tip: Use the complete owner/repository name.

templates.title: HTTPS endpoint references
templates.note: Look for URLs beginning with the scoped HTTPS host.
templates.tip: Repeat with a specific subdomain when the domain has several services.

templates.title: Domain in YAML configuration
templates.note: Review deployment and application configuration referencing the domain.
templates.tip: Example configuration can intentionally contain fictional infrastructure.

templates.title: Domain outside documentation paths
templates.note: Reduce matches whose path contains docs.
templates.tip: This is a path substring exclusion, not a guarantee that every result is application code.

templates.title: Domain without forked repositories
templates.note: Focus on repositories not marked as forks.
templates.tip: Compare with forks separately when tracking inherited configuration.

categories.title: Build & deployment
categories.lead: Map how a project is packaged and deployed by reviewing its published configuration.

templates.title: GitHub Actions workflows
templates.note: Review workflow definitions and deployment references.
templates.tip: Workflow names and environment labels help establish project context.

templates.title: Docker build files
templates.note: Locate files whose path includes Dockerfile.
templates.tip: Review base images, exposed ports and copied paths.

templates.title: Compose definitions
templates.query: repo:{repo} (path:compose.yml OR path:compose.yaml OR path:docker-compose.yml OR path:docker-compose.yaml)
templates.note: Find common Compose filenames.
templates.tip: Trace service names and bind mounts without assuming the examples are live deployments.
templates.global_query: (path:compose.yml OR path:compose.yaml OR path:docker-compose.yml OR path:docker-compose.yaml)

templates.title: Terraform configuration
templates.note: Discover infrastructure-as-code definitions.
templates.tip: Resource names describe intent; confirm the actual asset inventory separately.

templates.title: Deployment directory
templates.note: Inspect the deploy directory at the repository root.
templates.tip: Adapt the directory to the project layout.

templates.title: Domain in web-server configuration
templates.note: Find routing-related files mentioning the scoped domain.
templates.tip: Configuration may describe a development environment or an inactive service.

categories.title: Dependencies & implementation
categories.lead: Identify a project’s languages, packages and integration points.

templates.title: JavaScript package manifest
templates.note: Find the root JavaScript package manifest.
templates.tip: For a monorepo, remove the leading slash to include nested manifests.

templates.title: PHP package manifest
templates.note: Review the root Composer manifest.
templates.tip: Compare declared packages with the project documentation.

templates.title: Python project metadata
templates.note: Locate Python build and dependency metadata.
templates.tip: Some projects keep requirements in separate files instead.

templates.title: Go and Rust manifests
templates.note: Find module and crate manifests.
templates.tip: Nested manifests can reveal separate components.

templates.title: Package references in a lockfile
templates.note: Look for a chosen package or integration string.
templates.tip: Search absence is inconclusive: large or generated files may not be indexed.

templates.title: Term in a selected language
templates.note: Focus a content search on one language.
templates.tip: Use GitHub’s recognised language name.

categories.title: Documentation & project context
categories.lead: Use public project material to interpret technical findings and distinguish examples from deployed systems.

templates.title: Domain in README files
templates.note: Find README paths mentioning the scoped domain.
templates.tip: A link may be a citation or dependency rather than an owned endpoint.

templates.title: Term in project documentation
templates.note: Search a project’s root docs directory.
templates.tip: Try a broader path if documentation lives elsewhere.

templates.title: Published security guidance
templates.note: Locate public security-policy files.
templates.tip: Read the project’s current reporting instructions before contacting maintainers.

templates.title: Ownership and contribution guidance
templates.note: Locate files describing review responsibilities and contribution rules.
templates.tip: These are project-maintenance documents, not a complete organisation chart.

templates.title: Term in changelog files
templates.note: Find a named component or behaviour in published release notes.
templates.tip: A changelog entry can help identify the relevant release or migration.

templates.title: Domain in examples
templates.note: Separate demonstration references from production configuration.
templates.tip: Example values are not evidence of a live service.

categories.title: Repository discovery
categories.lead: Search project metadata and README text. These searches return repositories, not individual code matches.

templates.title: Public, non-archived projects
templates.note: List public repositories in the selected organisation that are not archived.
templates.tip: This does not imply active maintenance.

templates.title: Archived projects
templates.note: Review retired or preserved projects.
templates.tip: Historical configuration may no longer describe current infrastructure.

templates.title: Forked projects
templates.note: List repositories marked as forks.
templates.tip: Check the upstream project before attributing implementation choices.

templates.title: Term in project descriptions and READMEs
templates.note: Find a project by its name, description or README text.
templates.tip: Use code mode for arbitrary file content.

templates.title: Projects in a selected language
templates.note: Find projects by language with a modest popularity filter.
templates.tip: Stars help prioritise reading; they are not a quality or security score.

templates.title: Domain references in READMEs
templates.note: Find repositories whose README mentions the domain.
templates.tip: Search project code next to understand the relationship.

categories.title: Issues & pull requests
categories.lead: Follow public project discussions and changes with the separate issue-search syntax.

templates.title: Open issues about a term
templates.note: Find open discussions about a feature or component.
templates.tip: Read the full discussion to distinguish reports from confirmed behaviour.

templates.title: Domain in issue discussions
templates.note: Find a domain in issue bodies or comments.
templates.tip: A reported URL can belong to a test fixture or a third party.

templates.title: Open documentation issues
templates.note: Find organisation-wide issues with the documentation label.
templates.tip: Labels are project-defined; adjust the label for the repository.

templates.title: Merged changes mentioning a term
templates.note: Find merged pull requests describing a component or change.
templates.tip: Confirm the merge date and associated release before drawing conclusions.

templates.title: Pull requests awaiting required review
templates.note: Find open changes that still require review.
templates.tip: Review state is workflow information rather than a security assessment.

templates.title: Merged changes mentioning a domain
templates.note: Find merged pull requests whose description names the domain.
templates.tip: Issue search does not search the changed code; follow the PR to inspect its diff.

patterns.title: Content, not filenames
patterns.description: Name the content field when the string itself matters.

patterns.title: Two configuration formats
patterns.description: Group alternative file formats before adding the shared term.

patterns.title: Implementation without examples
patterns.description: Exclude an example path when reviewing implementation references.

patterns.title: Organisation, language and topic
patterns.description: Combine repository-level filters to narrow a project shortlist.

patterns.title: README discovery
patterns.description: Search project READMEs for a named domain, then inspect matching repositories.

patterns.title: Issue to merged change
patterns.description: Look for merged pull requests describing an issue’s topic.

guide.title: Choose the right search mode
guide.text: Code searches files; repository search finds projects; issue search covers issues and pull requests. Change modes before using a template from another category.

guide.title: Set a meaningful scope
guide.text: Start with an organisation or a complete owner/repository name. Domain mentions and copied code do not establish asset ownership.

guide.title: Open searches in your own GitHub session
guide.text: GitHub requires sign-in for code search, including public code. Githubify builds links and does not receive your GitHub login or access token.

guide.title: Understand code-search coverage
guide.text: Code search covers default branches and is not exhaustive. Generated, vendored, binary and oversized files can be absent. Queries are limited to 1,000 characters and results to 100; code-result sorting is unavailable.

guide.title: Read the context
guide.text: Inspect nearby code, README explanations and release information. A reference may be a tutorial, dependency, obsolete example or third-party endpoint.

guide.title: Keep evidence with the source
guide.text: Record a repository link and the relevant commit or file location in your own notes. Avoid copying private account data into shared screenshots or query exports.

guide.title: Adapt syntax deliberately
guide.text: Use content: and path: for modern website code search. Repository and issue modes have different fields. The REST code-search API also differs from the website search this tool targets.
